title: The 1/3–2/3 conjecture
statement: Every finite poset that is not a chain has incomparable elements x,y such that, among its linear extensions, both P(x<y) and P(y<x) are at least 1/3.

counterexample.description: A refutation is a poset for which, for every incomparable pair \(x,y\), either \(P(x<y)<1/3\) or \(P(y<x)<1/3\) over uniform linear extensions. Exact extension DP verifies it.
